mainTopic: Leftover communal offerings as קיץ המזבח, and which sins the goats of יום כיפור atone for
overview: The amud opens by finishing the teaching that leftover תמיד lambs are offered as קיץ המזבח, the altar's 'dessert.' The גמרא explains that 'white figs' is only a comparison, so it does not clash with the פסוק that bans fruit on the altar. It then explains why a bird עולה cannot be used for קיץ: leftovers go to communal gift offerings, and the community never brings birds. שמואל's rule that 'the knife' decides a communal offering's exact identity supports רבי יוחנן's teaching that surplus תמיד lambs can become קיץ המזבח. Two ברייתות about a שעיר that can move from one holiday to another back it up. The גמרא then returns to the משנה and learns from the words פשעים and חטאות that the inner goat of יום כיפור atones even for deliberate טומאת מקדש. Next, רב יהודה rereads the משנה's list of sins covered by the שעיר המשתלח so that no term repeats another. The amud ends with a sharp question: how can a plain missed עשה need יום כיפור at all? רבי זירא's answer begins on the next amud.

steps.title: Leftover lambs become 'dessert' for the altar
steps.stepSummary: The end of the teaching that surplus lambs are brought as קיץ המזבח, compared to white figs.
steps.simpleTranslation: They are brought as 'dessert,' like white figs, for the altar.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes a teaching that started on the previous amud. Lambs left over from the תמיד are brought as extra burnt offerings, called קיץ המזבח, the altar's 'dessert.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: קיץ means late-summer fruit, a dessert eaten after the meal. So when the altar has no other offerings, these extra עולות are brought to keep it from standing idle. The comparison to white figs will be questioned in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: Summer fruit or dessert. Here: extra offerings that keep the altar busy when it is otherwise idle
White figs, a kind of fig eaten as dessert

phrases.english: As dessert, like white figs, for the altar.
phrases.notes: The leftover תמיד lambs are what get offered as this 'dessert.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the teaching from the previous section about what is done with surplus תמיד lambs.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Surplus lambs are offered as קיץ המזבח, extra עולות brought as the altar's 'dessert.'

steps.title: Fruit cannot be offered on the altar
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how white figs can be connected to the altar when the תורה forbids offering any 'honey,' meaning fruit.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it is written: 'For any leaven and any honey' you may not burn on the altar!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the words 'white figs for the altar.' The תורה forbids putting fruit on the altar.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this פסוק, 'honey' includes fruit sweetness, so figs may never be burned on the altar. Read literally, 'white figs for the altar' sounds like figs are being offered, and that clashes with the פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: But it is written! (opens a challenge from a פסוק)
Honey. Here it includes sweet fruit

phrases.english: But isn't it written:
"For any leaven and any honey, etc."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 2:11. The rest of the פסוק says you may not burn these on the altar.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the wording 'white figs for the altar.'
steps.kashyaTarget: The phrase 'like white figs for the altar'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Fruit ('honey') is forbidden on the altar, so figs cannot be linked to the altar.

steps.title: The comparison is to figs for a person
steps.stepSummary: רב חנינא reads the line as a comparison: these offerings are to the altar what white figs are to a person.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חנינא taught: like white figs are for a person.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חנינא answers that no figs go on the altar at all. It is only a comparison.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just as a person eats white figs as dessert after a meal, these extra lambs are 'dessert' for the altar. The offerings are lambs, so the ban on fruit is not touched.

phrases.english: Rav Chanina teaches:
Like white figs for a person.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא by reading the phrase as a comparison.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Figs themselves were being linked to the altar.
steps.terutzMaskana: The lambs are to the altar what figs are to a person, a dessert. No fruit is offered.
steps.confusionAlert: Nobody ever put figs on the altar. 'White figs' is only a picture of what 'dessert' means.

steps.title: No bird offering for the altar's 'dessert'
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר רב חסדא teaches that a bird עולה is not used for קיץ המזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר רב חסדא taught publicly: We do not bring 'dessert' offerings with a bird burnt offering.
steps.whatsHappening: A new teaching: only animals, not a bird עולה, may be used as the altar's 'dessert.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: This limits what counts as קיץ המזבח. No reason is given yet, which is why רבא will attack it next.

keyTerms.meaning: A burnt offering of a bird

phrases.aramaic: דָּרַשׁ רַב נַחְמָן בַּר רַב חִסְדָּא:
phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Rav Chisda taught publicly:
We do not supply the altar's 'dessert' with a bird burnt offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: דָּרַשׁ רַב נַחְמָן בַּר רַב חִסְדָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a limit on which offerings may serve as קיץ המזבח.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A bird עולה is not used for קיץ המזבח.

steps.title: רבא calls the ruling nonsense
steps.stepSummary: רבא dismisses the ruling as a 'burkha,' something with no sense.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא strongly attacks רב נחמן בר רב חסדא's ruling and calls it foolish.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא sees no reason why a bird עולה could not keep the altar busy too. After all, it is also a burnt offering. He gives no proof, just rejects the ruling outright.

phrases.english: Rava said: This is nonsense!

steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that bird עולות are not used for קיץ
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A bird עולה is also a burnt offering, so there seems to be no reason to exclude it.

steps.title: The surplus is communal, and the community never brings birds
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק defends the ruling in the name of רב שימי מנהרדעא: surplus goes to communal gift offerings, and the community has no bird offerings.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said to רבא: What is nonsense about it? I told it to him, and I told it to him in the name of רב שימי מנהרדעא. For רב שימי מנהרדעא said: Leftovers go to the community's gift offerings, and there is no bird burnt offering for the community.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק explains that the ruling has a real source and a clear reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Leftover lambs belong to the community, so the קיץ offerings are communal gift offerings. The community never brings a bird עולה. So a bird cannot be used for קיץ.

keyTerms.meaning: A gift offering of the community

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק לְרָבָא:
phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said to Rava:
What is the nonsense?
I said it to him,
phrases.notes: 'I' is רב נחמן בר יצחק, and 'him' is רב נחמן בר רב חסדא.

phrases.aramaic: וּמִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב שִׁימִי מִנְּהַרְדְּעָא אַמְרִיתַהּ נִיהֲלֵיהּ –
phrases.english: and I said it to him in the name of Rav Shimi of Neharde'a,
as Rav Shimi of Neharde'a said:
Leftovers go to the community's gift offerings,
and there is no bird burnt offering for the community.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends step 4 against רבא's attack by giving its source and reason.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Giving the hidden reason behind the ruling
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ban on birds seemed to have no basis.
steps.terutzMaskana: קיץ offerings are communal offerings, and the community never brings a bird עולה.
steps.whatToRemember: קיץ המזבח is a communal offering, so it follows communal rules: animals only, never a bird.

steps.title: שמואל agrees: the knife decides a communal offering's identity
steps.stepSummary: שמואל holds like רבי יוחנן, since he rules that a communal offering's exact identity is set at slaughter.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל also holds like רבי יוחנן. For רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: Communal offerings — the knife draws them to what they are.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows that שמואל supports רבי יוחנן's idea that lambs set aside for the תמיד can be used for something else.
steps.deeperAnalysis: How can a lamb set aside for the תמיד be offered as קיץ? שמואל explains that setting aside a communal offering only puts it in a general group, like עולה. Its exact use is decided when it is slaughtered, 'by the knife.'

phrases.aramaic: וְאַף שְׁמוּאֵל סָבַר לְהָא דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן,
phrases.english: And Shmuel too holds like this teaching of Rabbi Yochanan,
phrases.notes: This is רבי יוחנן's earlier teaching that leftover תמיד lambs are used for the altar's 'dessert.'

phrases.english: as Rav Yehuda said in the name of Shmuel:
Communal offerings —
the knife draws them to what they are.
phrases.notes: Meaning: whatever it is slaughtered for decides which offering it becomes.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַף שְׁמוּאֵל סָבַר לְהָא דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to רבי יוחנן's main teaching and shows another אמורא shares its basic idea.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Communal offerings get their exact identity only when they are slaughtered.
steps.whyThisMatters: This principle explains why surplus communal animals can be moved from one use to another without a problem.

steps.title: A ברייתא: the goat can move between holidays
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows רבי שמעון agrees that a שעיר not offered on one day can be offered on another, supporting the idea that the knife decides.
steps.simpleTranslation: A ברייתא also teaches this: רבי שמעון agrees about the goat. If it was not offered on a רגל, it is offered on ראש חודש. If not on ראש חודש, on יום הכפורים. If not on יום הכפורים, on a רגל. If not on this רגל, on another רגל. This is because from the start it came only to atone on the outer altar.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that supports שמואל's rule. A goat set aside for one holiday's חטאת can be used on a different day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי שמעון holds that the goats of different days atone for different things. Still, he agrees that one goat can switch days. This is because when it was set aside it was only marked as a goat whose blood goes on the outer altar, and its exact purpose is set later, at slaughter.

keyTerms.meaning: A ברייתא also teaches this (a support)
Goat, here the communal חטאת goat
The outer altar, in the courtyard

phrases.english: It is also taught so:
And Rabbi Shimon agrees about a goat,
that if it was not offered on a festival
it may be offered on Rosh Chodesh,
and if it was not offered on Rosh Chodesh
it may be offered on Yom Kippur,
and if it was not offered on Yom Kippur
it may be offered on a festival,
and if it was not offered on this festival
it may be offered on another festival;
because from the start it came only
to atone on the outer altar.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא to back up שמואל's rule from step 7.
steps.raayaObject: שמואל's rule that a communal offering's identity is set at slaughter
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא where רבי שמעון lets a שעיר set aside for one day be offered on another
steps.whatToRemember: A communal offering is set aside only for a general purpose. Its exact use is decided at slaughter, so a leftover תמיד lamb can become קיץ, and a holiday goat can move to another day.

steps.title: Another teaching: the goat was set aside only for outer-altar atonement
steps.stepSummary: A short ברייתא adds that the חטאת goat was consecrated only to atone through the outer altar.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: it was consecrated only to atone through the outer altar.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings one more short ברייתא that backs up the previous step. It says the goat was set aside only to bring atonement through the outer altar.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The goat's purpose is outer-altar atonement in general, not one particular day. That fits the previous ברייתא, which said a goat not offered on one day can be offered on another.

keyTerms.meaning: Was consecrated, set aside as holy
The outer altar, in the courtyard

phrases.english: It was taught: it was not consecrated
phrases.notes: "It" means the חטאת goat being discussed in the previous steps.

phrases.english: except to atone
on the outer altar.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא: לֹא הוּקְדַּשׁ אֶלָּא לְכַפֵּר עַל מִזְבֵּחַ הַחִיצוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second ברייתא that supports the point of step 8.
steps.raayaObject: That the outer-altar goats share one general purpose and are not tied to a specific day.

steps.title: Where do we learn that the inner goat atones for deliberate טומאה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about the inner goat of יום כיפור and asks for its source.
steps.simpleTranslation: [The משנה said:] And for deliberate defilement of the מקדש and its holy foods, the goat whose service is done inside [atones], etc. From where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה, which said the inner goat of יום כיפור atones for deliberate טומאת מקדש וקדשיו. It asks where this comes from, setting up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now, the outer-altar goats were the topic. Now the focus moves to a new case: sins done on purpose, and the goat whose blood is brought inside the קודש הקדשים. The גמרא wants a פסוק as the source.

keyTerms.meaning: Entering the מקדש or eating holy food while טמא
The inner goat of יום כיפור, whose blood is brought inside
From where are these things known?

phrases.english: And for deliberate defilement of the Temple and its holy foods,
the goat performed inside, etc.
phrases.notes: "Etc." means the rest of the משנה line: this goat and יום כיפור itself bring the atonement.

phrases.english: From where are these matters derived?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the outer-altar goats and returns to a new clause of the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source that the inner goat atones for deliberate טומאת מקדש וקדשיו.

steps.title: The source: פשעים means rebellious sins, חטאות means accidental sins
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא reads ויקרא 16:16. The word פשעים means deliberate, rebellious sins, and חטאות means accidental sins, so the inner goat covers both.
steps.simpleTranslation: As the Rabbis taught: "And he shall atone for the קודש from the טומאות of בני ישראל," and so on. פשעים are rebellions, as it says "The king of מואב rebelled against me," and "Then לבנה rebelled at that time." חטאות are accidental sins, as it says "If a person sins by accident."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a ברייתא about the פסוק describing the inner goat. The פסוק says it atones for both פשעים and חטאות, and the ברייתא proves what each word means.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Other פסוקים use פשע for rebellion, like מואב and לבנה turning against their kings, so פשעים means sins done on purpose. חטא is used for accidental sins in ויקרא 4:2. Since the inner goat's פסוק lists both words, it atones for deliberate טומאת מקדש too.
steps.whatToRemember: The inner goat of יום כיפור covers deliberate טומאת מקדש because its פסוק says פשעים, which means rebellious, on-purpose sins.

phrases.english: As the Rabbis taught:
"And he shall atone for the Sanctuary
from the impurities of the children of Israel, etc.";
phrases.notes: ויקרא 16:16. The פסוק goes on: "and from their פשעים, for all their חטאות." Those are the two words explained next.

phrases.english: Pesha'im: these are the rebellious sins,
and so it says:
"The king of Moab rebelled against me,"
and it says: "Then Libnah rebelled at that time."
Chata'ot: these are the unintentional sins,
and so it says:
"If a person sins unintentionally."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 10 with a ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: ויקרא 16:16 lists פשעים (deliberate sins) for the inner goat, so it atones even for deliberate טומאת מקדש וקדשיו.

steps.title: The next line of the משנה: all other sins in the תורה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's next clause about all other sins, setting up the discussion of the שעיר המשתלח.
steps.simpleTranslation: [The משנה said:] For all other sins in the תורה, light and serious, deliberate and accidental, etc.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next part of the משנה. This step is a setup line that opens the next discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה moves from טומאת מקדש to every other kind of sin: light or serious, on purpose or by accident. The rest of the line, shortened here with "etc.," says the שעיר המשתלח atones for all of them.

phrases.english: For all other transgressions in the Torah,
the minor ones and the major ones,
the intentional ones and the unintentional ones, etc.
phrases.notes: The משנה continues with more kinds of sins and ends by saying the שעיר המשתלח atones for all of them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next clause of the משנה after finishing the source for the inner goat.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה's next clause: all other sins in the תורה, light or serious, deliberate or accidental, are covered (by the שעיר המשתלח).

steps.title: The משנה's list seems to repeat itself
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that the משנה's terms overlap: 'light' equals עשה and לא תעשה, 'severe' equals כרת and מיתות בית דין, 'made known' equals מזיד, and 'not made known' equals שוגג.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Light sins' are the same thing as positive and negative commandments! 'Severe sins' are the same thing as sins punished by כרת and by court death penalties! 'He was made aware' is the same as deliberate! 'He was not made aware' is the same as accidental!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה's wording. It says the list names the same categories twice under different labels.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה seems to list 'light and severe' and also 'עשה, לא תעשה, כרת, מיתות בית דין.' It also lists 'known and unknown' and also 'מזיד and שוגג.' If these pairs mean the same thing, why does the משנה say both?

keyTerms.meaning: Sins punished by כרת, being 'cut off' by Heaven
Death penalties carried out by the court
He was made aware (of the sin)

phrases.aramaic: הַיְינוּ קַלּוֹת הַיְינוּ עֲשֵׂה וְלֹא תַעֲשֶׂה!
phrases.english: Light sins are the same as positive and negative commandments!
phrases.notes: The משנה from step 12 lists both pairs, so the גמרא says one of them is extra.

phrases.aramaic: חֲמוּרוֹת – הַיְינוּ כָּרֵיתוֹת וּמִיתוֹת בֵּית דִּין!
phrases.english: Severe sins are the same as sins of karet and court death penalties!
'He was made aware' is the same as deliberate!
'He was not made aware' is the same as accidental!

steps.triggerLanguage: הַיְינוּ קַלּוֹת הַיְינוּ עֲשֵׂה וְלֹא תַעֲשֶׂה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the wording of the משנה clause quoted in step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: The list of sin categories in the משנה about the שעיר המשתלח.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Each pair of terms seems to mean the same thing as another pair, so the משנה looks repetitive.

steps.title: רב יהודה rereads the משנה so nothing is repeated
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה explains that the משנה means: light or severe, שוגג or מזיד. Among the שוגג cases, the doubt may or may not have become known to him. 'Light' and 'severe' are then defined as the עשה/לא תעשה and כרת/מיתות בית דין lists.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: This is what the משנה means. For all other sins in the תורה, whether light or severe, whether done accidentally or deliberately. And for the ones done accidentally, whether the doubt about them became known to him or did not become known to him. And these are the light ones: positive and negative commandments. And these are the severe ones: כרת and court death penalties.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה answers the challenge by rereading the משנה. Each phrase now adds new information instead of repeating.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Known / not known' is no longer the same as מזיד / שוגג. It now describes two kinds of accidental sins: ones where the doubt became known to him and ones where it did not. The list of עשה, לא תעשה, כרת and מיתות בית דין is now just a definition of 'light' and 'severe,' not an extra category.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what it means (a rereading of the text)
Their doubt, meaning whether he sinned at all

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the full range of sins covered by the שעיר המשתלח, which the next question about a plain עשה builds on.

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said: This is what it is saying:
For the other sins in the Torah,
whether light or severe,
whether he did them accidentally
or whether he did them deliberately.
Those that he did accidentally:
whether the doubt about them became known to him,
phrases.notes: Here 'known' now means he found out there was a question whether he sinned. It no longer means 'deliberate.'

phrases.english: or whether the doubt about them did not become known to him.

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵלּוּ הֵן קַלּוֹת – עֲשֵׂה וְלֹא תַעֲשֶׂה,
phrases.english: And these are the light ones: positive and negative commandments,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵלּוּ הֵן חֲמוּרוֹת – כָּרֵיתוֹת וּמִיתוֹת בֵּית דִּין.
phrases.english: and these are the severe ones: karet and court death penalties.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the redundancy challenge of step 13.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the משנה (הכי קאמר) so that each phrase has its own meaning.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה lists the same categories twice under different names.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Known / not known' refers to the doubt in accidental sins, and the specific list defines what 'light' and 'severe' mean.

steps.title: How can a missed positive מצוה need יום כיפור?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks about the עשה in the משנה. Without תשובה, an offering cannot help (זבח רשעים תועבה). With תשובה, he is forgiven right away on any day, as a ברייתא teaches.
steps.simpleTranslation: This positive commandment, what is the case? If he did not do תשובה, then 'the offering of the wicked is disgusting.' If he did do תשובה, then he is forgiven on any day too, as a ברייתא teaches: If someone broke a positive commandment and did תשובה, he does not move from there before he is forgiven.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the idea that the שעיר המשתלח is needed for a missed מצות עשה. Neither way of describing the case seems to work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Case one: no תשובה, so an offering cannot bring atonement because the פסוק calls it disgusting. Case two: he did תשובה, so the ברייתא says he is forgiven on the spot and does not need יום כיפור. Either way, the עשה seems to have no place in the משנה.

steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A two-way trap: without תשובה no offering works, and with תשובה forgiveness comes right away, so יום כיפור is not needed.
